## What it is

The record of each maintenance, repair and replacement activity on a system, local or nonlocal, with its approval, the people and escort, the tools, any removal and sanitization, and the control check afterward, plus the system's authorized maintenance personnel and approved maintenance tools, as SP 800-53 MA-2 requires.

## Preview (annotated)

:::note[Guidance]
Keep one log for each system, or one per facility for shared equipment such as printers and copiers, which NIST's MA-2 discussion includes. An organization with an IT service management system can keep the register there instead, as long as each record holds the fields below; for a High system, that is how MA-2(2) is usually met. Assessors sample the register against the maintenance schedule, the change records and remote access logs, and ask for the approval, the escort and the sanitization record behind each entry. The register at the end is also downloadable as a CSV file. Sections 2 and 3 are the lists that MA-5 and MA-3 require; keep them current here or link to where they are kept.
:::

### 1. How to use this log

- Schedule maintenance, repair and replacement as the manufacturer or vendor specifies and as organizational requirements add, and record each activity in the register (MA-2a).
- Get the system owner's approval before each activity starts, and record who monitored it (MA-2b).
- Include <span class="tpl-field tpl-param">Fill in: information to be included in organizational maintenance records <span class="tpl-typical">Typical: the date and time, the system and component, a description of the maintenance performed, the names and organization of the individuals performing it, the escort's name, the components or equipment removed or replaced, the approval, and the result of the post-maintenance control check</span></span> in each record (MA-2f).
- Record in the register the change request for any maintenance that changes the system's configuration (MA-2b, CM-3).
- Before a component leaves the facility for off-site maintenance, repair or replacement, get the explicit approval of <span class="tpl-field tpl-param">Fill in: personnel or roles required to explicitly approve the removal of the system or system components from organizational facilities for off-site maintenance or repairs <span class="tpl-typical">Typical: the system owner</span></span> (MA-2c), and sanitize its media to remove <span class="tpl-field tpl-param">Fill in: information to be removed from associated media prior to removal from organizational facilities for off-site maintenance, repair, or replacement <span class="tpl-typical">Typical: all organizational information, including personally identifiable information, credentials and cryptographic keys</span></span> (MA-2d). Record the sanitization record's ID. Keep storage media that cannot be sanitized, such as a failed drive, rather than sending them.
- After each activity, check the potentially impacted controls and record the result (MA-2e).
- The system owner reviews the register at least quarterly against the maintenance schedule and change records, and records the review in section 5 (MA-2a).
- Keep the log for <span class="tpl-field tpl-fill">Fill in: retention period from the organization's records retention schedule</span>.

| Field | What to record |
| --- | --- |
| Record ID | A unique ID for the activity |
| Start and end | Date and time the activity started and ended |
| Component | The system component or equipment serviced, with its inventory ID (CM-8) |
| Type | Scheduled, repair, replacement or diagnostic |
| Location | On site, nonlocal, or off site (removed from the facility) |
| Description | What was done, and why |
| Performed by | Names and organization of the individuals who performed it, and whether each is on the authorized list in section 2 (MA-5) |
| Escort or supervisor | Name of the person who escorted or supervised, or "not required" for authorized, unescorted personnel (MA-5c) |
| Approved by | Name and date of the approval before the activity (MA-2b), and the change request ID if one applies (CM-3) |
| Tools and media | Tools used, from section 3, with the result of the tool inspection and the media scan (MA-3, MA-3(1), MA-3(2)) |
| Nonlocal session | For nonlocal maintenance: how the person connected and authenticated, and when the session and connections ended (MA-4) |
| Removed or replaced | Components or equipment removed or replaced, with serial numbers; for removal, who approved it and the sanitization record ID (MA-2c, MA-2d); for maintenance equipment, how its removal was handled (MA-3(3)) |
| Control check | Controls checked after the activity, by whom, and the result (MA-2e) |

### 2. Authorized maintenance organizations and personnel

- Only the organizations and people on this list may perform maintenance on the system without an escort, and only after their access authorizations are verified (MA-5a, MA-5b).
- The system owner approves each addition and reviews the list at least quarterly (MA-5a).
- Anyone not on the list works only under the supervision of a designated escort with the required access authorizations and technical competence, with temporary credentials valid for that maintenance period only (MA-5c).

| Organization | Person | Maintenance performed | Access authorizations verified (screening, access agreement) | Local, nonlocal or both | Approved by and date | Contract or agreement | Review date |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |

:::note[Guidance]
For a High system, record here which people lack the clearances, citizenship or other access approvals the system's information requires, since MA-5(1) sets extra steps for them: supervision throughout by a qualified escort with the required access, volatile storage sanitized and nonvolatile media removed or disconnected beforehand, or the alternate controls in the MA-5(1) clause where that cannot be done.
:::

### 3. Approved maintenance tools

- Only the tools on this list may be used to maintain the system, by authorized maintenance personnel (MA-3a).
- Tools brought in or downloaded by maintenance personnel are inspected for improper or unauthorized modifications before each use, and media with diagnostic or test programs are scanned for malicious code before use (MA-3(1), MA-3(2)). Report a modified tool or infected media as a security incident.
- Review this list <span class="tpl-field tpl-param">Fill in: frequency at which to review previously approved system maintenance tools <span class="tpl-typical">Typical: at least annually</span></span> and remove tools that are outdated, unsupported, no longer needed or no longer used (MA-3b).
- Maintenance equipment containing organizational information leaves the facility only after it is verified to hold none, is sanitized or destroyed, or under a written exemption from <span class="tpl-field tpl-param">Fill in: personnel or roles who can authorize removal of equipment from the facility <span class="tpl-typical">Typical: the Chief Information Security Officer</span></span>; otherwise it stays (MA-3(3)).

### 4. Nonlocal maintenance

- Each nonlocal session is approved beforehand, monitored while it runs, and recorded in the register (MA-4a, MA-4d).
- Connections go through the organization's managed remote access service, with multi-factor, replay-resistant authentication, using only tools documented in the system security plan (MA-4b, MA-4c).
- Accounts that external maintenance providers use stay disabled except during an approved session (MA-4c).
- The session and network connections are ended when the maintenance is completed (MA-4e).
- For a High system, record for each provider the basis for concluding its maintenance system has comparable security; where it does not, remove, sanitize and afterward inspect the component instead (MA-4(3)).

<div class="tpl-federal">

#### Federal systems

[OMB M-22-09](https://www.whitehouse.gov/wp-content/uploads/2022/01/M-22-09.pdf) (January 26, 2022) requires phishing-resistant multi-factor authentication for agency staff, contractors and partners, and [OMB M-19-17](https://www.whitehouse.gov/wp-content/uploads/2019/05/M-19-17.pdf) (May 21, 2019), Section III, item 2, requires PIV credentials, where applicable in accordance with OPM requirements, as the primary means of authentication to Federal information systems by Federal employees and contractors; [OMB M-26-18](https://www.whitehouse.gov/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/M-26-18-Scaling-Use-of-Login.gov-to-Deliver-a-Universal-Sign-on-for-Public-Services.pdf) (August 31, 2026), footnote 5, lists both as existing OMB policy. CISA [Binding Operational Directive 23-02](https://www.cisa.gov/news-events/directives/binding-operational-directive-23-02) (June 13, 2023) requires agencies, within 14 days of discovery or of notice from CISA, to make the internet-exposed management interfaces of in-scope network devices reachable only from an internal enterprise network or only through a zero trust policy enforcement point separate from the interface. As of September 2026.

- For each nonlocal session, the register's "Nonlocal session" field shall record the phishing-resistant authenticator used, as OMB M-22-09 requires, and whether it was a PIV or derived PIV credential. (MA-4c)
- Where nonlocal maintenance uses the management interface of a device within the scope of BOD 23-02, the register shall record the internal network or policy enforcement point the session passed through. (MA-4b)

</div>
